clue.text: Female on record wearing fleece, a large number — here?

indicators.note: the shearing word wears the inner letters like a coat, so they go inside it

parts.note: to fleece a sheep is to shear it

indicators.note: in an across clue the female letter sits on, i.e. after, the record letters

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A woman on a record cover dressed in fleece, with a huge number of something around — where is she?
explanation.definitionFit: The definition plus wordplay point to the place where fleeces and big numbers of animals are found: an agricultural holding for flocks.

clue.text: Lute heard, however, as an old trombone

parts.note: lute spoken sounds like loot, and loot is plunder, a sack
however means but

explanation.surface: Someone mistakes the sound of a lute for an old brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lute heard' sounds like loot, which in turn means sack (plunder).
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance forerunner of the modern slide brass instrument.

clue.text: Tennis player and 15 side 11

definitions.note: here eleven means a team of eleven players, a football side

parts.note: Chris Evert, the American champion of the 1970s and 80s
15 is CRICKET; in cricket the leg side of the field is called the on side

explanation.surface: A tennis star joins a side for a team of eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle uses 11 both as a reference to BAT and as a plain number: here it is a football eleven. EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club fields a team of eleven, so a named club stands for an eleven.

clue.text: Source of fruit is lemon, say, with yellow centre to feed 11

definitions.note: 11 across is BAT, the flying mammal

parts.note: a pip is a seed, from which fruit comes

indicators.note: the centre letters are fed into the tree word

parts.note: a lemon is an example of a fruit tree

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word yellow

explanation.surface: A recipe telling you to stuff a lemon with yellow filling and give it to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes the middle two letters of the six-letter yellow; 11 here is the cross-reference to BAT, the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipistrelle is a small, common European species of the flying mammal referenced by 11.

clue.text: Applaud a goal, hugging Celtic's outside left

indicators.note: the outer words wrap around the inner letters as in an embrace

parts.note: an aim is a goal

indicators.note: take the first and last letters of Celtic

explanation.surface: Fans cheer a goal from Celtic's outside-left winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celtic's outside' gives C and C, the two ends of Celtic (the 's is the possessive).
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim someone is to praise them publicly, much as clapping does.

clue.text: Musical doctor covering ligatures and operatic overtures

indicators.note: the doctor word covers, i.e. goes around, the two starting letters

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: overtures are openings, so take the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A musically minded doctor watches an opera while tending to stitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtures' reads as opera openings, but it only means the first letters of ligatures and operatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something melodic is tuneful, which is one sense of musical.

clue.text: Miles 14 to 26, heading for glory that's brief!

indicators.note: miles fourteen to twenty-six are the second half, so only the back half of the word is kept

parts.note: the 26 miles of a race make up the marathon

indicators.note: take the first letter of glory

explanation.surface: A runner in the second half of a marathon chases glory wearing very little.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first half (MARA) of the race's name leaves THON.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are skimpy underpants and a thong is the skimpiest kind, so the answer is a minimal garment.

clue.text: Jack — knave put another way

indicators.note: the rogue's word is written the other way round

parts.note: a rat is a knave, a rogue

explanation.surface: The jack in a deck of cards is the knave by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and knave look like playing cards; Jack is really a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack and tar are both old slang words for a sailor.

clue.text: Diabolical brute getting on collar

parts.note: getting on means growing old
to collar and to nick are both slang for to arrest

explanation.surface: A fiendish beast is ageing and has been put in a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for the Devil, the diabolical one.

clue.text: Warm up, then cool bullet

indicators.note: then puts the second piece after the first
in a down clue the cosy word is read upwards

parts.note: snug means warm and cosy
cool and hot both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: Instructions for an engine: warm it up, then let it cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm up' gives GUNS, SNUG read upwards; 'cool' is fashionable, hot, not chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet fired from a weapon is a shot, and the gunshot is that discharge.

clue.text: How a bird goes for a song that's audible

indicators.note: the spoken word for inexpensive is matched by a word sounding the same

parts.note: bought for a song means cheap

explanation.surface: A bird's call is a song you can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheep is the thin high call of a small bird, the noise it goes.

clue.text: Academy acting to separate two points, literarily, for American statesman

indicators.note: the academy letters come between, separating, parts of the punctuation word

parts.note: the colon is the punctuation mark of two dots, in writing
RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art

explanation.surface: A grand title for a US politician split by dramatic training.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'statesman' as state's man: a man from a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Coloradan is a native of Colorado, so literally a man of an American state.

clue.text: See 15
Cold seafood bedecked stall?

definitions.meaning: cold here means aloof and unfriendly
a stall laden with seafood is, whimsically

explanation.surface: A frosty fishmonger whose stall is covered in seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stand-offish keeps others at a distance, which is cold in manner.

clue.text: Waste water redirected into river after a day

indicators.note: the river part follows the day

parts.note: FRI is short for Friday

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: water's letters are sent in a new direction, rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about water wasted when a river is diverted for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a day' is Friday, shortened; the Tay is a river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away money or time is to squander it bit by bit.

clue.text: Fit little time between function and drink

indicators.note: the short time letter sits between the two other pieces

parts.note: tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function
rum is a drink
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A brief fit between a work function and a drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of temper, a fit of rage.

clue.text: Two animals, one taken to the middle

definitions.meaning: a chirping insect followed by a flying mammal
the willow implement a batsman carries out to the middle, the pitch

explanation.surface: Two creatures, one of them carried into the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The middle' is cricket talk for the pitch in the centre of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman walks out to the middle carrying the wooden blade used to strike the ball.

clue.text: Don't talk about cryptic clue that's beyond question — sounds like that sucks?

indicators.note: the hush word goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the question letter
cryptic suggests the word clue is obscured, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about a fiendish clue: the noise of disapproval says it sucks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' looks like a homophone signal but belongs to the definition: the answer is a sucking sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A squelch is the wet sucking noise of a boot in mud, so it is a sound of that sort.

clue.text: Sage in fancy panties

indicators.note: fancy suggests the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wise person turns up wearing elaborate underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal word for wise, as a sage is.

clue.text: Different passage of tune, quality

indicators.note: passage of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical passage that differs in tone quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are not equal in size or amount are different from each other.

clue.text: After taking a spin, driver finally qualified — what? Cobblers!

indicators.note: the assembled letters are spun round to read backwards
take the last letter of driver

parts.note: able means competent, qualified
eh is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A learner driver spins the car, then passes: what nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers!' looks like an exclamation of disbelief (British slang for rubbish), but it means shoe menders. R + ABLE + EH reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel bar is a small shop or counter where cobblers repair shoes while you wait.

clue.text: Without family, around a hundred spies

indicators.note: the family phrase goes around the hundred letter

parts.note: having no family is to have no ties
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A lone agent among a hundred spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spies' looks like a plural noun but is the verb: sees.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy something is to catch sight of it, to observe.

clue.text: Savings banked in the branches?

definitions.meaning: money put aside for the future
a bird's clutch is laid up high in the trees, as if deposited in a bank's branches

explanation.surface: Savings deposited in bank branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum saved for later, like eggs kept in a nest.

clue.text: 11 more in the drink

indicators.note: the extra word sits in the tea word

parts.note: cha is tea, a drink
else means more, other

explanation.surface: Eleven more people fall in the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHELSEA is a London football club, so a team of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club fields a side of eleven players, so the club stands for the number.

clue.text: Marriage beginning to unravel, work to patch girl up

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole assembly is read upwards
the start letter and work are sewn into the girl word like a patch

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: take the first letter of unravel

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A marriage starts to come apart, and someone works to patch things up with the girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole patched-up word, not just the girl: the result reads upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spousal is the adjective for things of husband and wife, used like marriage in marriage vows.

clue.text: Newspapers covering second of February, last month, or the one before

indicators.note: the newspaper word covers, wraps around, the other letters

parts.note: the press is newspapers collectively

indicators.note: take the second letter of February

parts.note: DEC is December, the year's last month

explanation.surface: The papers cover late February and last month, or the time before that.
explanation.definitionFit: A predecessor is whoever held a post previously, the earlier one.

clue.text: Conscious element ending in grudge match

indicators.note: take the last letter of grudge

parts.note: colours that match go together, so match means go

explanation.surface: Pride is what really drives a grudge match.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian psychology the ego is the conscious part of the mind.

clue.text: Just English left, island heading backwards

parts.note: quit means left, departed

indicators.note: the island's name heads the other way, written in reverse

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: An Englishman left an island and headed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, which is just.

clue.text: Test score

definitions.meaning: to put to the test, have a go at
in rugby, a grounding of the ball over the line earns points

explanation.definitionFit: Try means attempt or test, and in rugby it is the main way to score points.

clue.text: 15 is no more, I should add

definitions.note: a fifteen, a rugby union team

parts.note: was is the past of is, so no longer is
PS, a postscript, adds a final note

explanation.surface: A death notice with a postscript tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 15 means a rugby fifteen, not the cross-reference; WASPS is an English rugby union club.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union club fields a team of fifteen players, so the club stands for the number.

clue.text: Match score

explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tally agree with each other, and a tally is also a running count of points.

clue.text: School prom that's a throwback?

parts.note: Rugby is a famous English public school
a prom is a formal dance, a ball

explanation.surface: A school dance that harks back to the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwback' is read literally: in rugby the ball may only be thrown backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing in rugby must go backwards, so the oval ball used is the thing thrown back.
